metadata.name: Maryland and Pennsylvania ("Ma & Pa") and its predecessors: Baltimore (North Avenue) - Delta - York, with the Delta - Peach Bottom branch
metadata.note: One main line drawn by era and operator (Rule 4 splits share geometry): Pennsylvania side York - Delta as Peach Bottom Railway (Middle Division, three staged legs 1874/1875/1876-1881), York and Peach Bottom 1883-1890, Baltimore and Lehigh 1891-1893, York Southern 1894-1900; Maryland side Baltimore - Delta as Maryland Central (three staged legs 1882/1883/1884-1890, Baltimore and Delta folded in), Baltimore and Lehigh 1891-1900; then the Maryland and Pennsylvania 1901-1954 end to end. Plus the Delta - Peach Bottom branch as a single 1893 [ANCHOR] under the Baltimore and Lehigh and the Preservation Society's Muddy Creek Forks motor-car rides 2018 [OPEN] - 2025 [OPEN].
metadata.year_boundaries: The report's drawable spans share their boundary years ([2] 1883-1891 and [3] 1891-1893; [4] -1901 and [9] 1901-; [7]/[8] -1891/1891-). The report's own ownership_split rule gives a transfer year to the company that ran most of it (1891 to the B&L from 5 May; 1901 to the Ma & Pa from 12 Feb), so the outgoing company is drawn to the year before and the line is not double-drawn: York and Peach Bottom and Maryland Central end 1890; York Southern and Baltimore and Lehigh (Maryland) end 1900. No passenger year is dropped - each boundary year is drawn under the incoming company. 1894 on the PA side is York Southern (by 30 June 1894), per the report.
metadata.company_names: 'Peach Bottom Railway' (Middle Division here, Eastern Division in lancaster_oxford_and_southern_railroad.geojson) is a DIFFERENT company from 'Peach Bottom Railroad' (the post-1881 Eastern Division company) - do not merge them with a Railway/Railroad-stripping normaliser. Maryland Central Railroad (1882-88) / Railway (1888-91) and Baltimore and Lehigh Railroad (1891-94) / Railway (MD, 1894-1901) are each ONE display company and one colour. 'Ma & Pa' is the well-known nickname of the Maryland and Pennsylvania; the formal display name is used in labels to read alongside its predecessors.
metadata.colour_choice: Peach Bottom Railway reuses its existing colour, pulled programmatically from data/lancaster_oxford_and_southern_railroad.geojson. New colours, checked unused by any company in data/ on 2026-10-23: York and Peach Bottom #9C2F3C, Maryland Central #5A7D2A, Baltimore and Lehigh #2E6B8F (both state halves), York Southern #C27C2C, Maryland and Pennsylvania #1F7A6E, Ma & Pa Railroad Preservation Society #7A3E6B.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN START: York and Peach Bottom drawn from 1883, the first positive passenger evidence (Dec 1883); 1882 passenger service after the 20 Dec 1881 sale is likely but unconfirmed. The PA Internal Affairs report for 1882 would settle it.
OPEN START and OPEN END: Preservation Society rides drawn 2018-2025 - earliest dated ride found Aug 2018, latest dated 2025; neither is a known start or end.

ANCHOR: Delta - Peach Bottom branch drawn for 1893 only (1893 Official Guide via Fowler). Passengers from the 1883 opening, the possible pre-1893 closure (AEG1894 'over five miles ... closed'), and any passenger year 1894-1903 are all unconfirmed.
York Southern / Baltimore and Lehigh Railway start: 1894 (WBL; PAIA1894) vs 1893 (MAPAHS). The B&L receiver reported on the road in April 1894; the exact sale date would fix the PA boundary.
Red Lion - Muddy Creek Forks probably carried passengers from Christmas 1874; the leg is drawn from 1875 because the Bridgeton opening date was not established.
Bel Air - Forest Hill likely opened in 1883 (contractors expected June 1883) but is confirmed only by Jan 1884; drawn from 1884.
1954 end: 31 Aug 1954 per AR, HMDB, EVG, WMPA; one marker says mail ran 'until September, 1954'. Year is 1954 either way.
No primary 1951 Ma & Pa schedule was read (the Feb 1952 Guide's Ma & Pa table is missing from the cached OCR; only its station index survives).
All headways and speeds are estimates (see each segment and speed_source).

Geometry: Forest Hill - Whiteford, Towson - Loch Raven, the Jones Falls - Stony Run - Towson stretches in Baltimore, and Dallastown - Ore Valley (original alignment) are unmapped; York terminal sites (York 1st and the Ma & Pa's York station) and the Peach Bottom branch junction and terminus are not pinned.
Mileage: WMPA's 44 + 34.8 division figures do not sum to its own 77.2; Fowler's mileposts are used.
metadata.omitted: Block [5] (Ma & Pa Pennsylvania Division) is drawn as part of the Ma & Pa main-line feature, not separately. Block [6] Baltimore and Delta (Apr - Aug 1882) is folded into the Maryland Central Baltimore - Towson feature and named in its note. Block [12] Dallastown spur: drawable NONE - omitted (no confirmable passenger year on the spur). Peach Bottom branch outside 1893: not drawn (no passenger evidence). Freight only, excluded (Rule 1): everything after 31 Aug 1954 (Baltimore - Whiteford to 1958; Whiteford - York to 1978/1984; York Railway remnants); York - Hanover (ex-PRR, bought 1976); the 1969 Peach Bottom power-plant line. Never operated, not drawn: the 1873 Maryland & Pennsylvania (Conowingo route), the Peach Bottom Railway Western Division, the Deer Creek and Susquehanna, the Maryland Central's threatened Pylesville - Peach Bottom branch.
metadata.horsecar_audit: None found - the Baltimore end opened in 1882 as a narrow-gauge steam road (EVG, AEG1882); nothing trimmed.
metadata.osm_notes: The road is tagged mainly historic:operator='Maryland and Pennsylvania Railroad' (TIGER-derived), not old_railway_operator; old_railway_operator='Maryland and Pennsylvania' appears only at North Avenue, on the Dallastown spur and on the Peach Bottom plant line. The Baltimore Light RailLink (old_railway_operator 'Maryland Electric'/PRR; the ex-Northern Central) and the York County Heritage Rail Trail (ex-NCR) were deliberately NOT used. Five railway=tram ways tagged old_railway_operator 'Maryland and Pennsylvania' at North Avenue are the Baltimore Streetcar Museum's 5 ft 4.5 in track on the old Ma & Pa yard/grade; used here only for alignment.

segments.note: 3-ft gauge steam from opening (no animal haulage; Rule 5 checked in the report). Peach Bottom Railway, chartered 1868, Middle Division (York - Delta); the same company as the Eastern Division drawn in lancaster_oxford_and_southern_railroad.geojson, hence the same colour. Passenger receipts were reported separately for the Middle Division to the PA Secretary of Internal Affairs for 1878, 1880 and 1881 (per the LO&S report). Fowler table 326 letters the stations Delta ... Dallastown, Ore Valley ... York (1st) 'y' = the 1876 Peach Bottom company public timetable. Ends 1881: receivership 1881, Middle Division sold 20 Dec 1881 and renamed York and Peach Bottom 17 March 1882; 1881 is a Peach Bottom Railway year. Service is believed to have continued under the new company, but 1882 is not drawn - see the York and Peach Bottom feature. York - Red Lion opened 4 July 1874: first rails 30 June 1874 and 'passenger service began July 4, 1874' (AR; WPBR citing Hilton). Headway is an ESTIMATE: no timetable was read for this era; 480 min assumes about two trains each way a day.
sources: Segment-level: opening 4 July 1874 per AR and WPBR (Hilton); 1878/1880/1881 Middle Division passenger receipts per the PA Internal Affairs reports read by the LO&S agent; end 1881 per AR (sale 20 Dec 1881) (as read and summarised in research/branches/maryland_and_pennsylvania_railroad.txt; not re-read by the tracer)

segments.note: York and Peach Bottom Railway (the Middle Division renamed 17 March 1882, AR; 'Railway' and 'Railroad' both used in the papers - one company). 3-ft gauge. START IS [OPEN]: 1883 is the first year with POSITIVE passenger evidence (Aegis & Intelligencer 14 Dec 1883: 'The York and Peach Bottom Railroad does not run Sunday trains', and through passenger rates with the Maryland Central under discussion). 1882 is NOT drawn: the road was in receivership/sale over the winter of 1881-82 and no 1882 passenger notice was found. Continuity from the Peach Bottom Railway is very likely but unproven - this is a withheld unknown, not a known gap; do not extend back to 1882 without evidence (the PA Internal Affairs report for 1882 would settle it). From 19 May 1889 through Baltimore - York passenger and express trains ran 'over the Maryland Central Railway and the York and Peach Bottom Railroad' (AEG1889; AR; WMC); the Maryland Central controlled the Y&PB by stock but the Y&PB kept its own board and president (McConkey), so 1889 is not an operator change. Ends 1890: merged into the Baltimore and Lehigh 5 May 1891, and the report gives a transfer year to the company that ran most of it, so 1891 is drawn as Baltimore and Lehigh. Headway is an ESTIMATE: no timetable was read for this era; 480 min assumes about two trains each way a day; 'does not run Sunday trains' (1883) is the only frequency evidence.
sources: Segment-level: 1883 passenger evidence per AEG1883b; 1889 through trains per AEG1889, AR and WMC; 1891 merger per AR and WBL (as read and summarised in research/branches/maryland_and_pennsylvania_railroad.txt; not re-read by the tracer)

segments.note: Pennsylvania half of the Baltimore and Lehigh Railroad, formed 5 May 1891 by merging the York and Peach Bottom with the Maryland Central (AR; WBL; WMC); one road Baltimore - York with through trains continuing from 1889. 3-ft gauge. Receiver Winfield J. Taylor from May 1893 (AEG1894) - receivership is not an operator change. Ends 1893: the PA portion was sold and reorganized as the York Southern within the year ending 30 June 1894 (PAIA1894; WBL '1894'; MAPAHS says 1893 - conflict recorded in metadata). The B&L receiver was still reporting on the road in April 1894, so the B&L ran the PA side for part of 1894; 1894 is drawn as York Southern, not both. The 1891-93 Baltimore - Delta half is the separate feature baltimore-and-lehigh-baltimore-delta (same company, same colour). Headway is an ESTIMATE: no timetable was read for this era; 480 min assumes about two trains each way a day.
sources: Segment-level: 1891 formation per AR, WBL and WMC; receivership May 1893 per AEG1894; 1894 sale per PAIA1894 and WBL (as read and summarised in research/branches/maryland_and_pennsylvania_railroad.txt; not re-read by the tracer)

segments.note: York Southern Railroad: bought the Pennsylvania portion of the Baltimore and Lehigh at the split sale and was reorganized by 30 June 1894 (PAIA1894; WBL '1894'; MAPAHS '1893'). Start 1894 is the year the company is proven to exist; its first EXPLICIT passenger evidence is July 1895, when 'two passenger engines of the broad-gauge pattern' were ordered for the conversion to standard gauge (AEG1895; standard gauge late 1895 per AR and WBL - a gauge change, not a split). A strict reading would start this at 1895. AEG1899 names York Southern employees and general manager Samuel M. Manifold; PAIA1899 lists 'York, Pa - Peach Bottom, Pa., 42.80' mi operated. Ends 1900: merged into the Maryland and Pennsylvania (company dates from 12 Feb 1901; PAIA1901 dates the York Southern's merger 26 Feb 1901), so 1901 is drawn as Ma & Pa. Headway is an ESTIMATE: no timetable was read for this era; 480 min assumes about two trains each way a day.

segments.note: The first months of this were run by the Baltimore and Delta Railway (formed 16 Dec 1878 from the Valley & Delta Narrow-Gauge and the Baltimore, Hampden & Towsontown), which opened Baltimore - Towson on 17 April 1882 'with eight round trips daily' (EVG; WMC) and merged into the Maryland Central in August 1882 (WMC). The Baltimore and Delta is folded into this Maryland Central feature rather than drawn as a separate April-August 1882 feature in its own colour. Steam from the start: a B&D baggage car derailed near Boundary Avenue in June 1882 (AEG1882) - no horsecar era on the Baltimore end (Rule 5 checked in the report). Maryland Central Railroad 1882-1888 (receiver William Gilmor from Oct 1884), sold 1888 and reorganized as the Maryland Central RAILWAY with Gilmor as president (WMC; AEG1888; AEG1891) - same display name, same management, same trains: not split. 3-ft gauge. Ends 1890: merged into the Baltimore and Lehigh 5 May 1891; 1891 is drawn as Baltimore and Lehigh. Headway is an ESTIMATE: 120 min is carried from the Baltimore and Delta's eight round trips a day at opening in 1882 (EVG); no Maryland Central timetable was read.

segments.note: Maryland and Pennsylvania Railroad ('Ma & Pa'): York Southern + Baltimore and Lehigh Railway, stockholders approved 2 Feb 1901, company dates from 12 Feb 1901 (AR; WMPA); the predecessors' trains continued. Whole line Baltimore (North Avenue) - York, 77.2 mi. Steam until gas-electric motor cars 61/62 took over most passenger work 1927-28; diesels from 1946; by 1951 'only one train remained' (EVG). Fowler's 1950 working-timetable stops (Hollywood, Towson Estates, Springwood Park) confirm 1950 passenger stops in both states; the Feb 1952 Official Guide still indexes Ma & Pa stations and 'North Avenue Station'. Ends 1954: the last passenger train ran Baltimore - York - Baltimore on 31 August 1954 after the mail contract was cancelled (AR; HMDB; EVG; WMPA; MAPAHS 'ended passenger service in both states'). No earlier passenger cut-back was found; the Baltimore - Whiteford / Whiteford - York split is a freight-era division. Afterlife, context only (Rule 1): Baltimore - Whiteford freight to 11 June 1958; PA division cut to York - Red Lion 1978, Red Lion section gone 1984; York remnants became York Railway (1999). Headway is an ESTIMATE: 480 min = the two round trips a day of 1901 (EVG); service fell to one round trip by 1951, which this single segment does not show.

Delta - start of the mapped grade is a straight leg. If drawn, it is a LATER alignment than its era for whatever stretch the plant line re-laid.

segments.note: [ANCHOR] - one proven year only. Delta - Peach Bottom (York County shore of the Susquehanna), 5.7 mi, built 1882-83 by the York and Peach Bottom as a slate and river/canal feeder (rails being laid June 1882, AEG1882; 'nearly built' 6 April 1883, AEG1883a; AR says opened March 1883). The ONLY positive passenger evidence is Fowler table 327's 'Peach Bottom z' - a station named Peach Bottom in the 1893 Official Guide - which falls in the Baltimore and Lehigh era, hence this company and colour. Service certainly ran wider than 1893 if it ran at all, but no other passenger year is confirmed: do not widen this anchor to look plausible, and do not delete it to tidy the map. LOW CONFIDENCE: the B&L receiver (from May 1893) 'opened over five miles of the railroad closed prior to his receivership' (AEG1894) - five-plus miles is this branch's length, so the branch may have been closed in early 1893 and the Guide listing may be dead. Still operated property of the York Southern in 1899 and the Ma & Pa in 1901-02 (PAIA1899/1901/1902) - property, not proof of passenger trains; abandoned 1 September 1903 (AR), an abandonment year, not a passenger end. No passenger evidence for the York and Peach Bottom, York Southern or Ma & Pa eras, so none of those is drawn. Headway 480 min is a placeholder ESTIMATE - nothing is known of the frequency.
